description: Fast bit manipulation extension methods for SByte, Byte, Int16, UInt16, Int32, UInt32, Int64 and UInt64: SetBit, SetBit0, SetBit1, ToggleBit, IsBitSet, Rol, Ror, ReverseBits, ReverseEndianness, PopCount, Parity, LeadingZeroCount, TrailingZeroCount, Log2, BitLength, IsPowerOfTwo, RoundUpToPowerOf2, ExtractLowestSetBit, ResetLowestSetBit, GetMaskUpToLowestSetBit, ExtractHighestSetBit, ZeroHighBits, ZeroLowBits, ParallelBitExtract (PEXT), ParallelBitDeposit (PDEP), Pack, Unpack, ZigZagEncode, ZigZagDecode, ToBitString. Backed by System.Numerics.BitOperations and hardware intrinsics (POPCNT, LZCNT, TZCNT, BMI1, BMI2, BSWAP, ARM RBIT) with automatic runtime fallback. Also includes an allocation-free bit packing layer over Span<byte>: BitPacking/BitWriter/BitReader for arbitrary width bit fields at any bit offset, and the variable length integer encodings built on them - VarInt (ULEB128, SLEB128, ZigZag), EbmlVInt (RFC 8794) and SizePrefix.
releaseNotes:
2.2.0: FIXED - ZeroHighBits returned different results on different target frameworks for an index outside 0 to the bit width of the type. On net6.0+ the Int32/UInt32/Int64/UInt64 overloads passed the index straight to BZHI, which reads only its low 8 bits, so ZeroHighBits(-1) kept the whole value instead of returning 0 and ZeroHighBits(256) returned 0 instead of keeping the value; the netstandard2.1 build and the SByte/Byte/Int16/UInt16 overloads implemented the documented behaviour. The index is now clamped before reaching the instruction, so every overload on every target matches the documentation. In-range indices are unaffected. FASTER - BitPacking, BitWriter and BitReader now read and write a field through a single 64 bit window instead of walking it one byte per iteration: a mixed width packet is 1.15x faster to write and 1.18x faster to read end to end, and individual wide fields up to 5.7x (read) / 6.5x (write). FASTER - EbmlVInt.Read derives the encoding length from LeadingZeroCount and the payload from one big endian load rather than two byte-at-a-time loops; the decode step is 1.7x faster for a 4 byte VINT and 5.3x for an 8 byte one, with 1 byte encodings unchanged on their own early path. Test suite grown from 430 to 487 tests.

2.1.0: New target framework - netstandard2.1 (.NET Core 3.x, Mono, Xamarin, Unity 2021+), alongside net6.0/net8.0/net10.0; System.Numerics.BitOperations and System.Runtime.Intrinsics uses are behind #if, so modern targets keep the intrinsic backed paths unchanged and netstandard2.1 uses portable implementations. Still no package dependencies. (.NET Framework does not support netstandard2.1 and stays on the 1.x line.) New bit packing layer over Span<byte> - BitPacking (arbitrary width bit fields at any bit offset, MSB first) plus BitWriter/BitReader ref structs for sequential packing. New variable length integer encodings in VarInt: ULEB128, SLEB128, ZigZag (Protocol Buffers sint) and the non-standard sign-magnitude format Tedd.SpanUtils writes. New EbmlVInt (RFC 8794 VINT, as used by Matroska/WebM) and SizePrefix (prefix-varint length field holding 30 bits in up to 4 bytes). New ZigZagEncode/ZigZagDecode extension methods.

2.0.0: BREAKING - now targets net6.0, net8.0 and net10.0 only; .NET Framework and .NET Standard consumers must stay on 1.x. Every operation is now backed directly by System.Numerics.BitOperations and hardware intrinsics (POPCNT, LZCNT, TZCNT, BMI1, BMI2, BSWAP, ARM64 RBIT). New: ToggleBit, Parity, TrailingZeroCount, Log2, BitLength, IsPowerOfTwo, RoundUpToPowerOf2, ExtractLowestSetBit, ResetLowestSetBit, GetMaskUpToLowestSetBit, ExtractHighestSetBit, ZeroHighBits, ZeroLowBits, ParallelBitExtract, ParallelBitDeposit, Rol/Ror for SByte/Byte/Int16/UInt16, plus SByte overloads throughout. Fixed: ReverseEndianness previously never took the intrinsic path due to an always-false compile constant and always ran the naive software fallback; it now always calls BinaryPrimitives.ReverseEndianness. Faster ReverseBits on x86/x64 (branch-free SWAR instead of table lookups).
